questions.q: Plants with weak stems that take the support of other objects to grow upwards are called ______.
questions.e: Climbers like the money plant and pea use tendrils or twining stems to climb on supports.

questions.q: A root system with one main root and smaller side roots is called a ______ root.
questions.e: A taproot has a main root from which lateral roots arise, as in mustard and neem.

questions.q: Rice and wheat are rich sources of which nutrient?
questions.e: Cereals like rice and wheat mainly provide carbohydrates (starch) that give us energy.

questions.q: Deficiency of vitamin C causes which disease?
questions.e: Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy, with bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds.

questions.q: The end of a freely suspended magnet that points towards the geographic north is called its ______ pole.
questions.e: The north-seeking end of a freely suspended magnet is called its north pole.

questions.q: The SI unit of length is the ______.
questions.e: The metre (m) is the SI unit of length.

questions.q: A material through which we can see objects clearly is called ______.
questions.e: Transparent materials like clear glass allow light to pass through completely.

questions.q: The normal temperature of the human body is about ______ °C.
questions.e: Normal human body temperature is about 37 °C (98.6 °F).

questions.q: The change of water vapour into liquid water on cooling is called ______.
questions.e: Droplets on the outside of a cold glass form by condensation of water vapour.

questions.q: Separating husk from grain with the help of wind is called ______.
questions.e: In winnowing the lighter husk is blown away by wind while heavier grains fall nearby.

questions.q: The process by which living beings produce young ones of their own kind is called ______.
questions.e: Reproduction allows living beings to produce offspring and continue their kind.

questions.q: Which gas makes up about 78% of the air?
questions.e: Air contains about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen.

questions.q: The star nearest to the Earth is the ______.
questions.e: The Sun is a star and it is the closest star to the Earth.

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.e: Mars looks reddish because of iron oxide (rust) in its soil.

questions.q: Plants whose leaves show net-like (reticulate) venation usually have which type of root?
questions.e: Leaves with reticulate venation are generally found in plants with taproots.

questions.q: A seed that has two cotyledons is called a ______ seed.
questions.e: Seeds like gram and pea have two cotyledons and are called dicots.

questions.q: When iodine solution is added to a food containing starch, the food turns ______ in colour.
questions.e: Starch gives a blue-black colour with dilute iodine solution.

questions.q: In the test for protein, adding copper sulphate and sodium hydroxide solutions to the food gives a ______ colour.
questions.e: A violet colour confirms the presence of protein.

questions.q: When the north pole of one magnet is brought near the north pole of another magnet, the two magnets ______.
questions.e: Like poles repel each other and unlike poles attract.

questions.q: Which of the following is attracted by a magnet?
questions.e: Iron is a magnetic material, while aluminium, plastic and rubber are non-magnetic.

questions.q: A pencil placed along a scale starts at the 1.0 cm mark and ends at the 13.5 cm mark. What is the length of the pencil?
questions.e: Length = 13.5 cm − 1.0 cm = 12.5 cm.

questions.q: The to-and-fro movement of a child on a swing is an example of ______ motion.
questions.e: Motion that repeats itself after a fixed interval of time is periodic motion.

questions.q: Substances like sugar and salt that disappear completely when stirred in water are said to be ______ in water.
questions.e: Sugar and salt dissolve completely in water, so they are soluble.

questions.q: A clinical thermometer usually measures temperatures from 35 °C up to ______ °C.
questions.e: A clinical thermometer has a range of about 35 °C to 42 °C because body temperature stays within it.

questions.q: At normal atmospheric pressure, water freezes into ice at ______ °C.
questions.e: Pure water freezes at 0 °C at normal atmospheric pressure.

questions.q: Separating insoluble solid particles from a liquid by passing it through filter paper is called ______.
questions.e: Filter paper lets the liquid pass but holds back the insoluble solid particles.

questions.q: Seeds need water, air and a suitable ______ to germinate.
questions.e: Seeds germinate even in the dark and without soil if water, air and suitable temperature are available.

questions.q: Living beings take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide during the process of ______.
questions.e: During respiration, food is broken down using oxygen to release energy and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Coal and petroleum, which take millions of years to form, are called ______ resources.
questions.e: Coal and petroleum are limited and cannot be replaced quickly, so they are non-renewable.

questions.q: The constellation that looks like a hunter with a belt of three bright stars is ______.
questions.e: Orion is easily recognised by the three stars in a row that form the hunter's belt.

questions.q: A bar magnet is broken into two pieces. How many poles will each piece have?
questions.e: Every piece of a magnet, however small, has both a north and a south pole.

questions.q: Ravi's handspan is 20 cm. He measures a table as 7 handspans long. What is the length of the table in cm?
questions.e: Length = 7 × 20 cm = 140 cm.

questions.q: Convert 2.5 km into metres.
Which of the following is translucent?
questions.e: Butter paper lets some light pass, so objects behind it look hazy; it is translucent.

questions.q: Convert 27 °C into kelvin (use K = °C + 273).
Wet clothes dry faster on a windy day because the wind increases the rate of ______.
questions.e: Wind carries away water vapour near the clothes, speeding up evaporation.

questions.q: Which method is used to obtain common salt from sea water?
questions.e: Sea water is left in shallow pits so that water evaporates and salt is left behind.

questions.q: To separate iron filings from a mixture of sand, salt and iron filings, the first step uses a ______.
questions.e: Iron is attracted by a magnet, so it can be removed first from the mixture.

questions.q: In the life cycle of a mosquito (egg, larva, pupa, adult), which stage comes immediately after the larva?
questions.e: The mosquito larva changes into a pupa, which then becomes an adult.

questions.q: Grass has fibrous roots. What type of leaf venation does it most likely have?
questions.e: Plants with fibrous roots usually have leaves with parallel venation.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.e: Sunlight is available continuously, so solar energy is renewable.

questions.q: The Moon is visible at night because it ______ sunlight falling on it.
questions.e: The Moon has no light of its own; it shines by reflecting sunlight.

questions.q: A child has bleeding gums and wounds that heal slowly. Foods rich in which vitamin should be added to the child's diet?
questions.e: Bleeding gums and slow healing are signs of scurvy, caused by lack of vitamin C (found in amla, oranges, lemons).

questions.q: A bicycle wheel covers 2 m on the road in one complete rotation. How many rotations will it make to cover 1 km?
questions.e: 1 km = 1000 m, so rotations = 1000 ÷ 2 = 500.

questions.q: Equal amounts of water at 40 °C and at 70 °C are mixed. What will be the approximate temperature of the mixture?
questions.e: For equal amounts the final temperature is about the average: (40 + 70) ÷ 2 = 55 °C.

questions.q: A mixture contains sand, common salt and water.
p: (a) Which method is used to remove the sand from the mixture?
(b) Which method is then used to recover the salt from the solution?
(c) The solid left behind on the filter paper is called the ______.
questions.e: Sand is insoluble and is removed by filtration (left as residue), while dissolved salt is recovered by evaporating the water.

questions.q: Water can exist as ice, liquid water and water vapour.
p: (a) At what temperature does ice melt at normal pressure?
(b) At what temperature does water boil at normal pressure?
(c) The change of liquid water into vapour at its boiling point is called ______.
questions.e: At normal pressure ice melts at 0 °C and water boils at 100 °C, changing into water vapour.

questions.q: A bar magnet is suspended freely with a thread so that it can rotate.
p: (a) In which direction does the magnet come to rest?
(b) Name the device based on this property that is used to find directions.
questions.e: A freely suspended magnet always rests in the north–south direction, which is the principle of the magnetic compass.

questions.q: Sky watchers use stars and constellations to find directions at night.
p: (a) Name the constellation of seven bright stars that looks like a big ladle or question mark.
(b) Name the star that appears stationary and shows the north direction.
questions.e: Ursa Major (Saptarishi) can be used to locate the Pole Star, which lies almost directly above the North Pole.

questions.q: A plant has leaves with parallel venation.
p: (a) What type of root system does it most likely have?
(b) How many cotyledons does its seed have?
questions.e: Plants with parallel venation are usually monocots, which have fibrous roots and one cotyledon in the seed.

questions.q: The natural indicator litmus is obtained from ______.
questions.e: Litmus is a dye extracted from lichens.

questions.q: An acidic solution turns blue litmus paper ______.
questions.e: Acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.q: A device used to open or close an electric circuit is called a ______.
questions.e: A switch completes or breaks the circuit to turn a device on or off.

questions.q: Materials that allow electric current to pass through them easily are called ______.
questions.e: Metals like copper and aluminium are good conductors of electricity.

questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called ______.
questions.e: Malleability lets metals like aluminium be beaten into foils.

questions.q: Which non-metal is stored under water because it catches fire in air?
questions.e: White phosphorus burns on exposure to air, so it is kept under water.

questions.q: Rusting of iron is a ______ change.
questions.e: Rust is a new substance (iron oxide) formed, so rusting is a chemical change.

questions.q: The period of life between childhood and adulthood is called ______.
questions.e: Adolescence is the stage of growth and change between childhood and adulthood.

questions.q: In solids, heat is mainly transferred by ______.
questions.e: In solids heat passes from particle to particle without the particles moving from their places, which is conduction.

questions.q: The SI unit of time is the ______.
questions.e: The second (s) is the SI unit of time.

questions.q: Digestion of food begins in the ______.
questions.e: Saliva in the mouth begins the digestion of starch.

questions.q: The tiny pores on the surface of leaves through which gases are exchanged are called ______.
questions.e: Stomata allow carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapour out of the leaf.

questions.q: Objects that do not allow any light to pass through them are called ______.
questions.e: Opaque objects block light completely and therefore form shadows.

questions.q: A solar eclipse occurs when the ______ comes between the Sun and the Earth.
questions.e: When the Moon blocks sunlight from reaching parts of the Earth, a solar eclipse occurs.

questions.q: Turmeric paper turns ______ in colour when dipped in a basic solution.
questions.e: Turmeric is yellow but turns red in basic solutions like soap solution.

questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base that forms salt and water is called ______.
questions.e: In neutralisation an acid and a base cancel each other's effect, producing salt and water.

questions.q: In a dry cell, the metal cap is the ______ terminal.
questions.e: The metal cap of a cell is its positive terminal and the flat metal base is the negative terminal.

questions.q: Which of the following is an insulator?
questions.e: Rubber does not allow electric current to pass, so it is an insulator.

questions.q: Metals produce a ringing sound when struck. This property is called ______.
questions.e: Sonority is why metals are used to make bells.

questions.q: Oxides of metals are generally ______ in nature.
questions.e: Metal oxides like magnesium oxide dissolve in water to form basic solutions.

questions.q: Depositing a layer of zinc on iron to prevent rusting is called ______.
questions.e: Galvanised iron pipes have a zinc coating that protects them from rusting.

questions.q: Obtaining large crystals of a pure substance from its solution is called ______.
questions.e: Pure crystals of salts like copper sulphate are obtained by crystallisation.

questions.q: The protruding front portion of the throat seen in boys during adolescence is called the ______.
questions.e: Growth of the voice box (larynx) in boys forms the Adam's apple and deepens the voice.

questions.q: The cool breeze that blows from the sea towards the land during the day is called ______.
questions.e: Land heats faster by day; warm air over land rises and cooler air from the sea moves in.

questions.q: Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth by ______.
questions.e: Radiation does not need a medium, so it can carry heat through empty space.

questions.q: A car covers 150 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.e: Speed = distance ÷ time = 150 km ÷ 3 h = 50 km/h.

questions.q: The time taken by a simple pendulum to complete one oscillation is called its ______.
questions.e: The time period of a pendulum is the time for one complete to-and-fro oscillation.

questions.q: The digestive juice in the stomach contains ______ acid.
questions.e: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach kills bacteria and helps protein digestion.

questions.q: Plants absorb water and minerals from the soil mainly through their ______.
questions.e: Root hairs increase the surface area of roots for absorbing water and minerals.

questions.q: In a plane mirror, the left side of an object appears as the right side of its image. This is called ______.
questions.e: Lateral inversion is why 'AMBULANCE' is written in reverse on ambulances.

questions.q: A train moves at a constant speed of 60 km/h. How far will it travel in 2.5 hours?
questions.e: Distance = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

questions.q: A simple pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 40 seconds. What is its time period?
questions.e: Time period = 40 s ÷ 20 = 2 s.

questions.q: Convert a speed of 72 km/h into m/s.
A solution does not change the colour of either red or blue litmus. The solution is ______.
questions.e: Neutral substances like sugar solution do not affect litmus.

questions.q: An ant bite injects formic acid into the skin. Which household substance is applied to relieve the pain?
questions.e: A mild base like baking soda neutralises the formic acid.

questions.q: In a circuit with a working cell and a closed switch, a bulb does not glow. The most likely broken part inside the bulb is its ______.
questions.e: If the filament is broken, the circuit is incomplete and no current flows through the bulb.

questions.q: When a magnesium ribbon burns in air, it forms a white powder called ______.
questions.e: Magnesium combines with oxygen of air to form magnesium oxide.

questions.q: Which of the following is a physical change?
questions.e: Melting changes only the state of wax; no new substance is formed.

questions.q: Cooking pans have handles of wood or plastic because these materials are poor ______ of heat.
questions.e: Wood and plastic do not conduct heat well, so the handles stay cool.

questions.q: Plants lose water in the form of vapour through stomata. This process is called ______.
questions.e: Transpiration also helps pull water up from the roots to the leaves.

questions.q: An eclipse in which the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon is called a ______ eclipse.
questions.e: When the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon, a lunar eclipse occurs.

questions.q: During vigorous exercise, the rate of breathing ______.
questions.e: Muscles need more oxygen during exercise, so we breathe faster.

questions.q: In which part of the alimentary canal is the digestion of food completed and the digested food absorbed into the blood?
questions.e: The small intestine completes digestion and its villi absorb digested food into the blood.

questions.q: A cyclist covers the first 10 km in 0.5 h and the next 20 km in 1.5 h. What is the average speed for the whole trip?
questions.e: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 30 km ÷ 2 h = 15 km/h.

questions.q: Two cells of 1.5 V each are connected in series (positive terminal of one joined to the negative terminal of the other). What is the total voltage of the battery?
questions.e: Voltages of cells in series add up: 1.5 V + 1.5 V = 3 V.

questions.q: A potted plant is kept in complete darkness for three days and then one of its leaves is tested with iodine.
p: (a) Will the leaf show the presence of starch? (yes/no)
(b) Which gas, along with water and sunlight, do leaves need to make food?
(c) Name the green pigment in leaves that traps sunlight.
questions.e: Without light there is no photosynthesis, so stored starch gets used up; photosynthesis needs carbon dioxide, water, sunlight and chlorophyll.

questions.q: Sulphur powder is burnt and the product formed is dissolved in water.
p: (a) Name the gas formed when sulphur burns in air.
(b) What colour does blue litmus turn in the solution formed?
(c) Hence, oxides of non-metals are generally ______ in nature.
questions.e: Sulphur dioxide dissolves in water to form sulphurous acid, showing that non-metal oxides are acidic.

questions.q: Vinegar is added to baking soda in a test tube and the gas produced is passed through lime water.
p: (b) What happens to the lime water?
(c) Is the reaction between vinegar and baking soda a physical or a chemical change?
questions.e: Vinegar reacts with baking soda to form new substances including carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky.

questions.q: A girl stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror.
p: (a) How far behind the mirror is her image?
(b) She moves 1 m towards the mirror. What is the distance between her and her image now?
questions.e: In a plane mirror the image is as far behind as the object is in front; at 1 m from the mirror the gap is 1 + 1 = 2 m.

questions.q: The Moon revolves around the Earth and shows different phases.
p: (a) What is the phase called when the Moon is not visible at all?
(b) The time between two successive full moons is about ______ days (to one decimal place).
questions.e: On the new moon day the lit half of the Moon faces away from us; the cycle of phases repeats in about 29.5 days.

questions.q: Microorganisms that cause diseases are called ______.
questions.e: Disease-causing microbes such as some bacteria and viruses are called pathogens.

questions.q: Which microorganism is used to make bread dough rise?
questions.e: Yeast respires and releases carbon dioxide, which makes the dough rise.

questions.q: Milk is converted into curd by the bacterium ______.
questions.e: Lactobacillus multiplies in milk and converts it into curd.

questions.q: Malaria is caused by a microorganism called ______.
questions.e: Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium.

questions.q: Malaria is spread by the female ______ mosquito.
questions.e: The female Anopheles mosquito carries Plasmodium from one person to another.

questions.q: A coil of insulated wire wound on an iron core that acts as a magnet only while current flows is called an ______.
questions.e: An electromagnet is a temporary magnet produced by electric current.

questions.q: A push or a pull on an object is called a ______.
questions.e: Any push or pull acting on an object is a force.

questions.q: The SI unit of force is the ______.
questions.e: Force is measured in newtons (N).

questions.q: The SI unit of pressure is the ______.
questions.e: Pressure is force per unit area, measured in pascals (1 Pa = 1 N/m²).

questions.q: In which state of matter are the particles packed most closely?
questions.e: Particles in a solid are tightly packed with very little space between them.

questions.q: A pure substance made up of only one kind of atom is called an ______.
questions.e: Elements like iron and oxygen contain only one kind of atom.

questions.q: In a salt solution, the salt is the ______.
questions.e: The substance that dissolves is the solute; the water in which it dissolves is the solvent.

questions.q: A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface bulges outwards is called a ______ mirror.
questions.e: A convex mirror has its reflecting surface curved outwards.

questions.q: The Earth takes about ______ hours to complete one rotation on its axis.
questions.e: One rotation of the Earth on its axis takes about 24 hours, giving us day and night.

questions.q: Rhizobium bacteria present in the root nodules of leguminous plants fix ______ from the air.
questions.e: Rhizobium converts atmospheric nitrogen into compounds plants can use.

questions.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.e: Common cold is viral; typhoid and tuberculosis are bacterial and malaria is protozoan.

questions.q: A vaccine protects us by helping the body produce ______ against a disease.
questions.e: Vaccines train the immune system to make antibodies so it can fight the real pathogen later.

questions.q: Dengue is spread by the bite of the ______ mosquito.
questions.e: The Aedes mosquito, which breeds in clean stagnant water, spreads dengue.

questions.q: A safety device in a circuit that melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows is a ______.
questions.e: A fuse wire melts due to the heating effect of excess current and protects appliances.

questions.q: The heating element of an electric heater or iron is commonly made of the alloy ______.
questions.e: Nichrome has high resistance and a high melting point, so it produces a lot of heat.

questions.q: The force of friction always ______ the motion of an object.
questions.e: Friction acts in the direction opposite to the motion or attempted motion.

questions.q: The force with which the Earth pulls every object towards itself is called ______ force.
questions.e: Gravitational force makes objects fall towards the Earth.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.e: A magnet can attract iron from a distance without touching it.

questions.q: The pressure exerted by a liquid ______ with depth.
questions.e: That is why dams are made thicker at the bottom.

questions.q: The calm, low-pressure central region of a cyclone is called its ______.
questions.e: The eye of a cyclone is a calm area surrounded by strong winds and clouds.

questions.q: The spreading of particles of one substance among the particles of another on their own is called ______.
questions.e: The smell of perfume spreading across a room is due to diffusion.

questions.q: Water is a ______ of hydrogen and oxygen.
questions.e: In water, hydrogen and oxygen are chemically combined in a fixed ratio.

questions.q: A solution in which no more solute can be dissolved at a given temperature is called a ______ solution.
questions.e: A saturated solution already holds the maximum solute possible at that temperature.

questions.q: The point at which rays parallel to the principal axis meet after reflection from a concave mirror is called the ______.
questions.e: Parallel rays converge at the principal focus of a concave mirror.

questions.q: A calendar based on the phases of the Moon is called a ______ calendar.
questions.e: A lunar calendar counts months by the cycle of the Moon's phases.

questions.q: A force of 100 N acts uniformly on an area of 2 m². What is the pressure?
questions.e: Pressure = force ÷ area = 100 N ÷ 2 m² = 50 Pa.

questions.q: A box weighing 600 N rests on the floor on a base measuring 0.5 m × 0.4 m. What pressure does it exert on the floor?
questions.e: Area = 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2 m², so pressure = 600 ÷ 0.2 = 3000 Pa.

questions.q: School bags have wide straps because a larger area ______ the pressure on the shoulders.
questions.e: For the same force, pressure is less when it acts on a larger area.

questions.q: Two forces of 5 N and 3 N act on a box in opposite directions. What is the net force on the box?
questions.e: Forces in opposite directions subtract: 5 N − 3 N = 2 N.

questions.q: In which state of matter is diffusion the fastest?
questions.e: Gas particles move fastest and have the most space between them, so they diffuse fastest.

questions.q: Air is a ______ of gases (element, compound or mixture).
questions.e: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen and other gases mixed in varying proportions without chemical combination.

questions.q: 20 g of sugar is completely dissolved in 180 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
questions.e: Mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent = 20 g + 180 g = 200 g.

questions.q: The amount of most solid solutes that can dissolve in water ______ with increase in temperature.
questions.e: Solubility of most solids, like sugar, increases when water is heated.

questions.q: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.e: A convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image and gives a wider field of view.

questions.q: A lens that is thicker at the centre than at the edges is called a ______ lens.
questions.e: A convex lens is thicker in the middle and converges light rays.

questions.q: When current flows through a wire placed near a magnetic compass, the compass needle ______.
questions.e: A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field that deflects the compass needle.

questions.q: Pickles and jams keep for long because salt and sugar prevent the growth of ______.
questions.e: Salt and sugar draw water out of microbes, so they cannot grow and spoil the food.

questions.q: 15 g of salt is dissolved in 85 g of water. What is the concentration of the solution as a mass percentage?
Which mirror forms an enlarged and erect image of a face held very close to it, and is used as a shaving mirror?
questions.e: When the object is between the pole and focus, a concave mirror forms an enlarged, erect, virtual image.

questions.q: The Earth takes about 365.25 days to go around the Sun, but a calendar year has 365 days. After how many years is one extra day added to keep the calendar correct?
questions.e: 0.25 day × 4 = 1 day, so an extra day is added every 4 years (a leap year).

questions.q: A brick of size 0.2 m × 0.1 m × 0.05 m weighs 20 N.
p: (a) What is the area of its largest face?
(b) What pressure does it exert when resting on its largest face?
(c) On which face (largest or smallest) should it rest to exert the maximum pressure?
questions.e: Largest face = 0.2 × 0.1 = 0.02 m², so pressure = 20 ÷ 0.02 = 1000 Pa; the smallest area gives the greatest pressure.

questions.q: An electric bell works using an electromagnet.
p: (a) The core of the electromagnet is made of soft ______.
(b) What happens to the magnetism of the electromagnet when the current is switched off?
questions.e: Soft iron becomes a magnet only while current flows and loses its magnetism as soon as the current stops.

questions.q: Yeast is added to sugar solution and kept in a warm place for a few hours.
p: (a) Name the process by which yeast converts sugar into alcohol.
(b) Which gas is released during this process?
questions.e: Yeast ferments sugar into alcohol and carbon dioxide, a process discovered by Louis Pasteur.

questions.q: Iron filings and sulphur powder are mixed (sample A). Part of the mixture is heated strongly to form a black mass (sample B).
p: (a) Is sample A a mixture or a compound?
(b) Name the substance formed in sample B.
(c) Can iron be separated from sample B using a magnet? (yes/no)
questions.e: In the mixture iron keeps its magnetic property, but on heating it combines with sulphur to form the compound iron sulphide.

questions.q: A boy pushes a box along the floor with a force of 50 N while friction acts on it with a force of 30 N.
p: (a) What is the net force on the box?
(b) If friction increases to 50 N, what is the net force on the box?
questions.e: Friction acts opposite to the push, so net force = 50 − 30 = 20 N, and becomes 50 − 50 = 0 N when they are equal.

questions.q: The change of a solid directly into vapour without passing through the liquid state is called ______.
questions.e: Camphor and ammonium chloride sublime on heating.

questions.q: The SI unit of temperature is the ______.
questions.e: Temperature is measured in kelvin (K) in the SI system.

questions.q: A homogeneous mixture of a metal with another metal or non-metal, such as brass, is called an ______.
questions.e: Alloys like brass (copper and zinc) cannot be separated by physical methods but have variable composition.

questions.q: One atomic mass unit is defined as exactly one-twelfth of the mass of one atom of ______-12.
questions.e: The carbon-12 isotope is the standard reference for atomic masses.

questions.q: Which scientist proposed that matter is made of tiny indivisible particles called atoms?
questions.e: John Dalton put forward the atomic theory of matter.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle did J.J. Thomson discover?
questions.e: J.J. Thomson discovered the negatively charged electron.

questions.q: The neutron was discovered by ______.
questions.e: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

questions.q: Which cell organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.e: Mitochondria release energy in the form of ATP.

questions.q: The plant tissue that transports water and minerals from roots to leaves is ______.
questions.e: Xylem conducts water and minerals upward; phloem carries food.

questions.q: The SI unit of acceleration is ______.
questions.e: Acceleration is change in velocity per second, so its unit is m/s².

questions.q: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of ______.
questions.e: The first law describes inertia, the tendency of a body to resist change in its state of motion.

questions.q: The acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface is about ______ m/s².
questions.e: The value of g near the Earth's surface is about 9.8 m/s².

questions.q: The SI unit of work is the ______.
questions.e: Work is measured in joules; 1 J = 1 N × 1 m.

questions.q: Sound cannot travel through a ______.
questions.e: Sound needs a material medium to travel, so it cannot pass through a vacuum.

questions.q: The heat energy required to change 1 kg of a solid into liquid at its melting point is called the latent heat of ______.
questions.e: Latent heat of fusion is absorbed without any rise in temperature.

questions.q: Convert 300 K into the Celsius scale (use °C = K − 273).
The scattering of a beam of light by colloidal particles is called the ______ effect.
questions.e: The Tyndall effect is seen when sunlight passes through a dense forest canopy or a dusty room.

questions.q: A solution contains 40 g of common salt in 360 g of water. What is its concentration as mass by mass percentage?
Calculate the molecular mass of H<sub>2</sub>O (H = 1 u, O = 16 u).
questions.e: Molecular mass = 2 × 1 + 16 = 18 u.

questions.q: Write the chemical formula of aluminium oxide.
questions.e: Aluminium has valency 3 and oxygen valency 2; criss-crossing gives Al₂O₃.

questions.q: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of ______ in the nucleus of its atom.
questions.e: Atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.q: Atoms of the same element having the same atomic number but different mass numbers are called ______.
questions.e: Protium, deuterium and tritium are isotopes of hydrogen.

questions.q: Which cell organelle is known as the 'suicide bag' of the cell?
questions.e: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes that can digest the cell itself if it is damaged.

questions.q: The movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution is called ______.
questions.e: Osmosis is the special case of diffusion of water through a selectively permeable membrane.

questions.q: The connective tissue that connects a muscle to a bone is called a ______.
questions.e: Tendons are strong, less flexible fibrous tissues joining muscles to bones; ligaments join bone to bone.

questions.q: A car starting from rest reaches a velocity of 20 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
What is the momentum of a 2 kg ball moving with a velocity of 3 m/s?
questions.e: Momentum p = m × v = 2 × 3 = 6 kg m/s.

questions.q: An object has a mass of 60 kg on the Earth. What will be its mass on the Moon?
questions.e: Mass is the quantity of matter and does not change from place to place.

questions.q: A force of 10 N moves an object through 5 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
The number of oscillations of a sound wave per second is called its ______.
questions.e: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), the number of oscillations per second.

questions.q: A car moving at 15 m/s applies brakes and stops in 3 s with uniform retardation. What distance does it travel while stopping?
questions.e: Distance = average velocity × time = (15 + 0)/2 × 3 = 22.5 m.

questions.q: An athlete runs one complete round of a 400 m circular track and stops at the starting point. What is the athlete's displacement?
questions.e: Displacement is the shortest distance between initial and final positions, which coincide here.

questions.q: What force is needed to give a car of mass 1500 kg an acceleration of 2 m/s²?
A 5 g bullet is fired from a 2 kg gun with a velocity of 400 m/s. What is the recoil velocity of the gun?
questions.e: By conservation of momentum, 0.005 × 400 = 2 × v, so v = 1 m/s.

questions.q: What is the weight of a 10 kg object on the Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²)?
If the distance between two objects is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes ______ of its original value.
questions.e: Gravitational force varies as 1/d², so doubling d makes the force 1/2² = 1/4.

questions.q: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving with a velocity of 5 m/s?
questions.e: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 5² = 25 J.

questions.q: A motor does 6000 J of work in 30 s. What is its power?
A sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. What is its speed?
questions.e: v = frequency × wavelength = 500 × 0.68 = 340 m/s.

questions.q: A person hears an echo of a clap 2 s after clapping. If the speed of sound is 340 m/s, how far is the reflecting wall?
questions.e: Sound travels to the wall and back: distance = (340 × 2) ÷ 2 = 340 m.

questions.q: A desert cooler cools better on a hot, dry day because dry air increases the rate of ______.
questions.e: Evaporation absorbs heat, and it is faster when humidity is low.

questions.q: Which type of muscle, found only in the heart, shows rhythmic contraction throughout life?
questions.e: Cardiac muscles are involuntary and contract and relax rhythmically all through life.

questions.q: A car travels the first 30 km at 60 km/h and the next 30 km at 30 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.e: Time = 0.5 h + 1 h = 1.5 h, so average speed = 60 km ÷ 1.5 h = 40 km/h.

questions.q: A 2 kg ball is dropped from a height of 20 m. Ignoring air resistance, what is its kinetic energy just before it hits the ground (g = 10 m/s²)?
questions.e: All potential energy changes to kinetic energy: mgh = 2 × 10 × 20 = 400 J.

questions.q: Calculate the formula unit mass of CaCl<sub>2</sub> (Ca = 40 u, Cl = 35.5 u).
questions.e: Formula unit mass = 40 + 2 × 35.5 = 111 u.

questions.q: A car of mass 1000 kg moving at 10 m/s is brought to rest uniformly in 5 s by applying brakes.
p: (a) What is the magnitude of its retardation?
(b) What is the magnitude of the braking force?
(c) What was the initial momentum of the car?

questions.q: An object weighs 588 N on the Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²). The gravity on the Moon is one-sixth of that on the Earth.
p: (a) What is the mass of the object?
(b) What will be its weight on the Moon?
questions.e: m = 588 ÷ 9.8 = 60 kg, and weight on the Moon = 588 ÷ 6 = 98 N.

questions.q: An atom contains 11 protons and 12 neutrons.
questions.e: Atomic number = protons = 11 (sodium), and mass number = protons + neutrons = 23.

questions.q: A ship sends an ultrasonic signal to the sea bed and receives the echo after 4 s. The speed of sound in sea water is 1500 m/s.
p: (a) What total distance does the signal travel?
(b) What is the depth of the sea?
questions.e: Total distance = 1500 × 4 = 6000 m; the signal goes down and back up, so depth = 6000 ÷ 2 = 3000 m.

questions.q: Choose the separation technique for each mixture.
p: (a) Acetone and water (miscible liquids with a large difference in boiling points)
(b) Different coloured dyes in black ink
questions.e: Distillation separates miscible liquids by boiling point, chromatography separates dyes, and sublimation separates a sublimable solid.

questions.q: A reaction in which a single reactant breaks down to give simpler products is called a ______ reaction.
questions.e: For example, calcium carbonate decomposes on heating into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: The slow eating away of metals by the action of air, moisture or chemicals is called ______.
questions.e: Rusting of iron and the black coating on silver are examples of corrosion.

questions.q: What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
questions.e: Pure water is neutral and has a pH of 7.

questions.q: What is the chemical name of baking soda?
questions.e: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃.

questions.q: Which is the only metal that is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.e: Mercury is a liquid metal; bromine is a liquid non-metal.

questions.q: Compounds made up of only carbon and hydrogen are called ______.
questions.e: Methane, ethane and ethene are hydrocarbons.

questions.q: In which cell organelle does photosynthesis take place?
questions.e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which absorbs light energy.

questions.q: The basic filtration unit of the human kidney is the ______.
questions.e: Each kidney has a large number of nephrons that filter blood.

questions.q: The junction between two neurons, across which a nerve impulse passes, is called a ______.
questions.e: At a synapse, chemicals carry the impulse from one neuron to the next.

questions.q: Amoeba reproduces asexually by ______.
questions.e: Amoeba splits into two daughter cells by binary fission.

questions.q: Which scientist performed experiments on garden pea plants and is called the father of genetics?
questions.e: Gregor Mendel worked out the basic rules of inheritance using pea plants.

questions.q: The SI unit of the power of a lens is the ______.
questions.e: Power of a lens in dioptres is 1 ÷ focal length in metres.

questions.q: The defect of vision in which a person can see nearby objects clearly but not distant objects is called ______.
questions.e: In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina.

questions.q: The SI unit of electrical resistance is the ______.
questions.e: Resistance is measured in ohms (Ω).

questions.q: Fe + CuSO<sub>4</sub> → FeSO<sub>4</sub> + Cu is an example of a ______ reaction.
questions.e: Iron, being more reactive, displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.

questions.q: A substance that gains oxygen during a reaction is said to be ______.
questions.e: Gain of oxygen (or loss of hydrogen) is oxidation.

questions.q: What is the chemical formula of bleaching powder?
questions.e: Bleaching powder (CaOCl₂) is made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime.

questions.q: Plaster of Paris is obtained by heating ______ at 373 K.
questions.e: Heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) at 373 K gives Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O).

questions.q: The chief ore of aluminium is ______.
questions.e: Aluminium is extracted from bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O) by electrolysis.

questions.q: A chemical bond formed by the transfer of electrons from a metal to a non-metal is called an ______ bond.
questions.e: Transfer of electrons forms oppositely charged ions held by ionic (electrovalent) bonds.

questions.q: What is the general formula of alkanes?
questions.e: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

questions.q: The –OH functional group is present in which class of carbon compounds?
questions.e: Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is an alcohol containing the –OH group.

questions.q: Name the enzyme present in saliva that breaks down starch.
questions.e: Salivary amylase breaks down starch into sugar in the mouth.

questions.q: Which hormone secreted by the pancreas regulates blood sugar level?
questions.e: Insulin lowers blood sugar; its deficiency causes diabetes.

questions.q: Which plant hormone promotes cell division?
questions.e: Cytokinins promote cell division and are present in fruits and seeds.

questions.q: The fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete is called ______.
questions.e: Fertilisation forms a zygote that develops into a new organism.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is present in human males?
questions.e: Human males have one X and one Y chromosome; females have XX.

questions.q: A concave mirror has a radius of curvature of 30 cm. What is its focal length?
questions.e: Focal length = R ÷ 2 = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm.

questions.q: The splitting of white light into its seven component colours by a prism is called ______.
questions.e: Different colours bend by different angles in a prism, causing dispersion.

questions.q: A potential difference of 12 V across a conductor drives a current of 3 A through it. What is its resistance?
What is the power of a convex lens of focal length 50 cm?
An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 15 cm. At what distance from the lens is the image formed?
questions.e: Using 1/v − 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/15 − 1/30 = 1/30, so v = 30 cm on the other side.

questions.q: What is the magnification produced by a plane mirror?
questions.e: A plane mirror forms an erect image of the same size, so m = +1.

questions.q: Resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in series. What is the equivalent resistance?
questions.e: In series, R = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω.

questions.q: Two resistors of 6 Ω each are connected in parallel. What is their equivalent resistance?
An electric bulb draws a current of 0.5 A from a 220 V supply. What is its power?
In the balanced equation __Fe + 4H<sub>2</sub>O → Fe<sub>3</sub>O<sub>4</sub> + 4H<sub>2</sub>, what is the coefficient of Fe?
questions.e: Fe₃O₄ has 3 iron atoms, so 3 Fe are needed on the left side.

questions.q: A solution turns red litmus blue. Its pH is ______ than 7.
questions.e: Bases turn red litmus blue and have pH greater than 7.

questions.q: Which gas is evolved when a metal like zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.e: Active metals displace hydrogen from dilute acids; the gas burns with a pop sound.

questions.q: How many single covalent bonds are present in a molecule of methane (CH<sub>4</sub>)?
questions.e: Carbon shares one electron pair with each of the four hydrogen atoms.

questions.q: Which rule gives the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field?
questions.a: Fleming's left-hand rule|Fleming left hand rule|left-hand rule|left hand rule|Fleming's left hand rule
questions.e: In Fleming's left-hand rule the forefinger shows the field, middle finger the current and thumb the force.

questions.q: In human lungs, exchange of gases between air and blood takes place in tiny air sacs called ______.
questions.e: Alveoli provide a large surface surrounded by blood capillaries for gas exchange.

questions.q: A myopic person cannot see objects beyond 2 m clearly. What is the power of the lens needed to correct this defect?
questions.e: A concave lens of f = −2 m is needed, so P = 1/f = −0.5 D.

questions.q: An electric heater of 1000 W is used for 2 hours every day. How much electrical energy does it consume in 30 days?
questions.e: Energy = 1 kW × 2 h × 30 = 60 kWh.

questions.q: Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) and pure dwarf (tt) pea plants and self-pollinated the F1 plants. What is the ratio of tall to dwarf plants in the F2 generation?
questions.e: F2 gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt; three of these four are tall, so the ratio is 3 : 1.

questions.q: An object 4 cm tall is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm.
p: (a) How far from the mirror is the image formed?
(b) What is the height of the image (ignore the sign)?
(c) Is the image real or virtual?
questions.e: With u = −20 cm and f = −10 cm, 1/v = 1/f − 1/u gives v = −20 cm and m = −1, so a real, inverted image of the same size forms at C.

questions.q: Resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in series to a 10 V battery.
p: (a) What is the total resistance of the circuit?
(b) What current flows in the circuit?
(c) What is the potential difference across the 6 Ω resistor?

questions.q: Lead nitrate solution is mixed with potassium iodide solution.
p: (a) What is the colour of the precipitate formed?
(c) What type of reaction is this?
questions.e: Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KI → PbI₂ (yellow precipitate) + 2KNO₃ is a double displacement (precipitation) reaction.

questions.q: Ethanol is warmed with alkaline potassium permanganate solution.
p: (b) What type of reaction is this?
(c) Ethanol reacts with this product in the presence of an acid catalyst to give a sweet-smelling compound called an ______.
questions.e: Alkaline KMnO₄ oxidises ethanol to ethanoic acid, which reacts with ethanol (esterification) to form a sweet-smelling ester.

questions.q: A long straight conductor carries an electric current vertically upwards.
p: (a) Which rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around the conductor?
right-hand thumb rule|right hand thumb rule|Maxwell's corkscrew rule
(b) The magnetic field lines around the conductor are ______ circles.
questions.e: The field lines are concentric circles around the wire, and their direction is given by the right-hand thumb rule.

questions.q: Respiration is an ______ reaction because energy is released in it.
questions.e: Glucose combines with oxygen in our cells and releases energy, so respiration is exothermic.

questions.q: Quicklime (calcium oxide) reacts vigorously with water to form slaked lime. What is the chemical name of slaked lime?
questions.e: CaO + H<sub>2</sub>O → Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> + heat. Slaked lime is calcium hydroxide.

questions.q: When fats and oils in food are oxidised, the food becomes ______ and its smell and taste change.
questions.e: This is rancidity. It is slowed by adding antioxidants or by filling food packets with nitrogen.

questions.q: During the electrolysis of water, the volume of gas collected at the cathode is double the volume collected at the anode. Which gas is collected at the cathode?
questions.e: 2H<sub>2</sub>O → 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub>, so twice as much hydrogen as oxygen is produced; hydrogen collects at the cathode.

questions.q: White silver chloride turns grey in sunlight as it breaks down into silver and chlorine. This decomposition is caused by ______.
questions.e: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl<sub>2</sub> in sunlight. This reaction is used in black and white photography.

questions.q: What is the colour of ferrous sulphate crystals before they are heated?
questions.e: FeSO<sub>4</sub>·7H<sub>2</sub>O crystals are green. On heating they lose water and then decompose into Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>, SO<sub>2</sub> and SO<sub>3</sub>.

questions.q: In the reaction CuO + H<sub>2</sub> → Cu + H<sub>2</sub>O, which substance is reduced?
questions.e: Copper oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced; hydrogen gains oxygen, so it is oxidised. This is a redox reaction.

questions.q: In the balanced equation 2H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O, how many molecules of water are formed from 4 molecules of hydrogen?
questions.e: Hydrogen and water are in the ratio 2 : 2, so 4 molecules of hydrogen give 4 molecules of water.

questions.q: Sodium sulphate solution is mixed with barium chloride solution and a white insoluble solid, barium sulphate, forms. What is such an insoluble solid formed in a reaction called?
questions.e: Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> + BaCl<sub>2</sub> → BaSO<sub>4</sub>↓ + 2NaCl is a double displacement reaction that gives a white precipitate.

questions.q: Calcium oxide is added to water.
p: (b) Is this reaction exothermic or endothermic?
(c) A solution of this product is used for ______ walls.
questions.e: CaO + H<sub>2</sub>O → Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> + heat. On the wall, calcium hydroxide reacts slowly with carbon dioxide in the air to form a shiny layer of calcium carbonate.

questions.q: Which acid is produced in the human stomach and helps in digestion?
questions.e: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid. Too much of it causes acidity, which is treated with an antacid.

questions.q: The sting of a bee or an ant injects ______ acid into the skin.
questions.e: The sting contains methanoic acid. Rubbing a mild base such as baking soda on it gives relief.

questions.q: Washing soda has the formula Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>·10H<sub>2</sub>O. What is its chemical name?
questions.e: Washing soda is sodium carbonate with ten molecules of water of crystallisation.

questions.q: The reaction between an acid and a base that gives a salt and water is called ______.
questions.e: For example, NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H<sub>2</sub>O.

questions.q: Which gas is produced when an acid reacts with a metal carbonate?
questions.e: Metal carbonate + acid → salt + carbon dioxide + water. The gas turns lime water milky.

questions.q: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth falls below ______.
questions.e: Bacteria in the mouth produce acids from food particles; below pH 5.5 tooth enamel starts to corrode.

questions.q: The electrolysis of brine (a solution of sodium chloride) is called the ______ process, after the products it gives.
questions.e: It gives chlorine and hydrogen gases and sodium hydroxide (an alkali), hence chlor-alkali.

questions.q: Two solutions have pH 3 and pH 6. What is the pH of the solution with the higher concentration of hydrogen ions?
questions.e: The lower the pH, the higher the hydrogen ion concentration, so the pH 3 solution is more acidic.

questions.q: Dry hydrogen chloride gas does not change the colour of dry blue litmus paper, because acids produce hydrogen ions only in the presence of ______.
questions.e: HCl forms H<sup>+</sup> (H<sub>3</sub>O<sup>+</sup>) ions only in water, so dry HCl gas does not behave as an acid.

questions.q: How many molecules of water of crystallisation are present in one formula unit of blue copper sulphate crystals?
questions.e: The formula is CuSO<sub>4</sub>·5H<sub>2</sub>O. On heating, the crystals lose this water and turn white.

questions.q: Baking powder is used to make cakes soft and spongy.
p: (a) Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda and a mild edible acid such as ______ acid.
(b) Which gas, released on heating or mixing with water, makes the cake rise?
questions.e: Sodium hydrogencarbonate reacts with the acid (H<sup>+</sup>) to give carbon dioxide, which makes the cake rise; the acid also removes the bitter taste of sodium carbonate.

questions.q: Gold and silver can be hammered into very thin foils. This property of metals is called ______.
questions.e: Gold and silver are the most malleable metals.

questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be drawn into thin wires is called ______.
questions.e: Gold is the most ductile metal; copper and aluminium are drawn into wires for electrical use.

questions.q: Which non-metal, a form of carbon, is a good conductor of electricity?
questions.e: Graphite conducts electricity, while diamond, another form of carbon, does not.

questions.q: Sodium and potassium are stored under ______ to stop them catching fire in air.
questions.e: They react so vigorously with oxygen and water that they catch fire if kept in the open.

questions.q: Most metal oxides, such as sodium oxide and magnesium oxide, are ______ in nature.
questions.e: Metal oxides are generally basic; non-metal oxides are generally acidic.

questions.q: Oxides such as aluminium oxide and zinc oxide, which react with both acids and bases, are called ______ oxides.
questions.e: Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> reacts with HCl to form a salt and water, and with NaOH to form sodium aluminate and water.

questions.q: A freshly prepared mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in the ratio 3 : 1 is called ______.
questions.e: Aqua regia (royal water) can dissolve gold and platinum.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy of copper and ______.
questions.e: Brass is copper and zinc; bronze is copper and tin; solder is lead and tin.

questions.q: In the thermit reaction, aluminium reduces ______ to give molten iron, which is used to join railway tracks.
questions.e: Fe<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + 2Al → 2Fe + Al<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> + heat.

questions.q: Heating a carbonate ore strongly in a limited supply of air, to change it into an oxide, is called ______.
questions.e: ZnCO<sub>3</sub> → ZnO + CO<sub>2</sub>. Sulphide ores are instead roasted in excess air.

questions.q: How many electrons does a magnesium atom (atomic number 12) lose to form a magnesium ion, Mg<sup>2+</sup>?
questions.e: Magnesium (2, 8, 2) loses its two outer electrons to get the stable configuration 2, 8.

questions.q: Impure copper is purified by electrolytic refining, using acidified copper sulphate solution as the electrolyte.
p: (a) Is the impure copper made the anode or the cathode?
(b) On which electrode is pure copper deposited?
(c) The insoluble impurities that settle below the anode are called anode ______.
questions.e: Copper dissolves from the impure anode and pure copper is deposited on the thin pure copper cathode; impurities collect as anode mud.

questions.q: A carbon atom has four electrons in its outermost shell. What is the valency of carbon?
questions.e: Carbon shares its four valence electrons to form four covalent bonds, so it is tetravalent.

questions.q: Compounds that have the same molecular formula but different structures are called ______.
questions.e: For example, butane (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>) has a straight-chain and a branched-chain isomer.

questions.q: Diamond and graphite are two ______ of carbon.
questions.e: Allotropes are different forms of the same element; fullerenes are another allotrope of carbon.

questions.q: The ability of carbon atoms to bond with other carbon atoms and form long chains is called ______.
questions.e: Catenation and tetravalency together explain the very large number of carbon compounds.

questions.q: Successive members of a homologous series differ by a ______ unit.
questions.e: Each member differs from the next by CH<sub>2</sub>, which is 14 u in mass.

questions.q: Hydrocarbons that contain a carbon–carbon double bond are called ______.
questions.e: Ethene (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>) is the simplest alkene; alkynes have a triple bond.

questions.q: Vegetable oils are changed into vegetable ghee by adding hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst. This reaction is called ______.
questions.e: Hydrogenation is an addition reaction that turns unsaturated fats into saturated ones.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of CH<sub>3</sub>COOH?
questions.e: It has two carbon atoms (eth-) and the carboxylic acid group (-oic acid). Its common name is acetic acid.

questions.q: How many covalent bonds are there in a molecule of ethane, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>?
questions.e: There are 6 C–H bonds and 1 C–C bond, so 7 covalent bonds in all.

questions.q: Which gas is given off when ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate?
questions.e: 2CH<sub>3</sub>COOH + Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub> → 2CH<sub>3</sub>COONa + H<sub>2</sub>O + CO<sub>2</sub>.

questions.q: Soaps clean oily dirt from clothes.
p: (a) In water, soap molecules gather into clusters with the oily dirt in the centre. What are these clusters called?
(b) Soap does not lather well in ______ water, which contains calcium and magnesium salts.
questions.e: The ionic end of a soap molecule faces the water and the hydrocarbon tail holds the oil, forming micelles. In hard water, soap forms an insoluble scum instead.

questions.q: Tiny pores on the surface of leaves, through which gases are exchanged, are called ______.
questions.e: Stomata also lose water by transpiration; guard cells open and close them.

questions.q: Which plant tissue carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves?
questions.e: Xylem carries water and minerals; phloem carries food.

questions.q: The red pigment in red blood cells that carries oxygen is ______.
questions.e: Haemoglobin has a high affinity for oxygen and carries it from the lungs to the tissues.

questions.q: The transport of food from the leaves to other parts of a plant is called ______.
questions.e: Translocation takes place in the phloem and uses energy from ATP.

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.e: Two atria and two ventricles keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate.

questions.q: Bile juice is made by which organ?
questions.e: Bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder; it breaks fats into small globules.

questions.q: In yeast, the breakdown of glucose without oxygen produces carbon dioxide and ______.
questions.e: This anaerobic respiration is called fermentation.

questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart to the organs of the body?
questions.e: Arteries have thick, elastic walls because blood leaves the heart under high pressure.

questions.q: During vigorous exercise, a lack of oxygen in muscle cells changes pyruvate into ______, which causes cramps.
questions.e: Without enough oxygen, pyruvate is converted to lactic acid in the muscles.

questions.q: Finger-like projections on the inner wall of the small intestine, which increase the surface area for absorbing food, are called ______.
questions.e: Villi are richly supplied with blood vessels that take the absorbed food to every cell.

questions.q: In humans, blood passes through the heart twice in one complete cycle. This is called ______ circulation.
questions.e: Blood goes heart → lungs → heart → body → heart, which keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood separate.

questions.q: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis.
p: (a) Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
(c) Which green pigment absorbs light energy?
questions.e: 6CO<sub>2</sub> + 12H<sub>2</sub>O → C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> + 6O<sub>2</sub> + 6H<sub>2</sub>O, in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll.

questions.q: Proteins are digested partly in the stomach.
p: (a) Name the enzyme in gastric juice that digests proteins.
(b) Which acid in the stomach provides the acidic medium this enzyme needs?
questions.e: Gastric glands release hydrochloric acid, pepsin and mucus; the mucus protects the stomach lining from the acid.

questions.q: The basic structural and functional unit of the nervous system is the ______.
questions.e: A neuron has dendrites, a cell body and an axon.

questions.q: Which part of the brain maintains the posture and balance of the body?
questions.e: The cerebellum, in the hind-brain, coordinates posture, balance and precise voluntary movements.

questions.q: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make which hormone?
questions.e: A lack of iodine can cause goitre, a swollen neck; iodised salt helps prevent it.

questions.q: A quick, automatic response to a stimulus, such as pulling your hand away from a hot object, is called a ______ action.
questions.e: Reflex actions happen without thinking, which protects the body from harm.

questions.q: The pathway taken by nerve impulses in a reflex action is called a reflex ______.
questions.e: In a reflex arc, impulses travel from a receptor to the spinal cord and back to a muscle.

questions.q: Which hormone, secreted by the adrenal glands, prepares the body to deal with an emergency?
questions.e: Adrenaline makes the heart beat faster and sends more blood to the muscles.

questions.q: The movement of a plant shoot towards light is called ______.
questions.e: Shoots bend towards light; roots generally bend away from it.

questions.q: Which part of the brain controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting?
questions.e: The medulla, in the hind-brain, controls these involuntary actions.

questions.q: The growth of a pollen tube towards the ovule is an example of ______.
questions.e: The pollen tube grows in response to chemicals from the ovule.

questions.q: Which plant hormone inhibits growth and causes leaves to wilt?
questions.e: Abscisic acid is a growth-inhibiting hormone.

questions.q: Dwarfism results from a lack of which hormone, secreted by the pituitary gland, in childhood?
questions.e: Growth hormone controls growth and development of the body.

questions.q: When light falls on a growing shoot from one side, the hormone auxin moves to the ______ side, so the shoot bends towards the light.
questions.e: Auxin makes the cells on the shaded side grow longer, so the shoot bends towards the light.

questions.q: The leaves of the touch-me-not plant (Mimosa) fold up when touched.
p: (a) Does this movement depend on growth? Answer yes or no.
(b) The plant cells change shape by changing the amount of ______ in them.
questions.e: Electrical and chemical signals pass from cell to cell, and the cells lose water and change shape, so the leaves fold without any growth.

questions.q: Yeast reproduces asexually by ______.
questions.e: A small bud grows out of the parent yeast cell and separates.

questions.q: Bread mould (Rhizopus) reproduces by ______ formation.
questions.e: Spores are formed in sporangia; they have thick walls and grow when they reach a moist surface.

questions.q: The male reproductive part of a flower is the ______.
questions.e: The stamen makes pollen grains; the pistil is the female part.

questions.q: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma is called ______.
questions.e: Pollination can happen within the same flower (self) or between flowers (cross).

questions.q: The malaria parasite, Plasmodium, divides into many daughter cells at the same time. This is called ______ fission.
questions.e: In multiple fission one cell divides into many; in binary fission it divides into two.

questions.q: Spirogyra breaks up into smaller pieces, each of which grows into a new individual. This is called ______.
questions.e: Fragmentation is common in simple multicellular organisms such as Spirogyra.

questions.q: Planaria can grow into a complete organism from a small piece of its body. This ability is called ______.
questions.e: Specialised cells grow and form the missing parts.

questions.q: Growing new plants from the roots, stems or leaves of a parent plant is called ______ propagation.
questions.e: Layering, grafting and cutting are methods of vegetative propagation.

questions.q: In human females, fertilisation usually takes place in the ______.
questions.e: The egg meets the sperm in the oviduct; the zygote then implants in the uterus.

questions.q: After fertilisation in a flower, the ovary develops into the ______.
questions.e: The ovary grows into a fruit, and the ovules inside it become seeds.

questions.q: In human males, the sperm are produced in the ______.
questions.e: The testes also make the hormone testosterone.

questions.q: A developing embryo gets nutrition from the mother's blood through a special tissue called the ______.
questions.e: The placenta has villi that give a large surface for passing glucose and oxygen to the embryo.

questions.q: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes does a human egg cell have?
questions.e: Gametes have half the number of chromosomes, so the zygote formed at fertilisation has 46 again.

questions.q: After fertilisation in a flower, the parts change.
p: (b) The zygote divides many times to form the ______ inside the seed.
questions.e: The zygote becomes the embryo, the ovule becomes the seed and the ovary becomes the fruit.

questions.q: Sections of DNA that carry the information for a characteristic are called ______.
questions.e: Genes are carried on chromosomes and control characteristics by making proteins.

questions.q: In Mendel's experiments, the trait that appears in the F1 generation is called the ______ trait.
questions.e: When pure tall and pure dwarf plants were crossed, all F1 plants were tall, so tallness is dominant.

questions.q: A trait that is hidden in the F1 generation but reappears in the F2 generation is called a ______ trait.
questions.e: Dwarfness disappeared in F1 and reappeared in a quarter of the F2 plants.

questions.q: The sex of a child is decided by the chromosome inherited from the ______.
questions.e: The mother always passes on an X chromosome; the father passes on either an X (girl) or a Y (boy).

questions.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are there in a human body cell?
questions.e: Human body cells have 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs, including one pair of sex chromosomes.

questions.q: Genes are made of ______.
questions.e: DNA in the chromosomes carries the information for making proteins.

questions.q: Characteristics passed on from parents to offspring through genes are called ______ traits.
questions.e: Traits gained during life, such as a skill or an injury, are acquired and are not passed on.

questions.q: Which pair of sex chromosomes is present in human females?
questions.e: Females have two X chromosomes, so every egg carries an X chromosome.

questions.q: Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) pea plants with pure dwarf (tt) plants. What percentage of the F1 plants were tall?
questions.e: Every F1 plant was Tt, and because tallness is dominant, all of them were tall.

questions.q: A pea plant with genotype Tt is crossed with a dwarf plant (tt). What percentage of the offspring are expected to be tall?
questions.e: The offspring are Tt and tt in equal numbers, so half are tall.

questions.q: In Mendel's monohybrid cross, what percentage of the F2 plants are pure tall (TT)?
questions.e: F2 gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt: one in four is TT.

questions.q: Mendel crossed pea plants with round yellow seeds (RRYY) and wrinkled green seeds (rryy). In what ratio did the four kinds of seeds appear in the F2 generation?
questions.e: The F2 gives 9 round yellow, 3 round green, 3 wrinkled yellow and 1 wrinkled green, showing that the two traits are inherited independently.

questions.q: In pea plants, round seed (R) is dominant over wrinkled seed (r). A plant with genotype Rr is self-pollinated.
p: (a) What percentage of the offspring are expected to have wrinkled seeds?
(b) How many different genotypes appear among the offspring?
questions.e: Rr × Rr gives RR, Rr, Rr and rr: three genotypes, and only rr (one in four) has wrinkled seeds.

questions.q: According to the laws of reflection, the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of ______.
questions.e: Also, the incident ray, the normal and the reflected ray lie in the same plane.

questions.q: Which type of mirror do dentists use to see large images of teeth?
questions.e: A tooth held between the pole and the focus of a concave mirror gives an enlarged, erect image.

questions.q: A lens that is thicker in the middle than at the edges is a ______ lens.
questions.e: A convex lens converges parallel rays of light to a point.

questions.q: The speed of light in a vacuum is 3 × 10<sup>8</sup> m/s. What is its speed in a medium of refractive index 1.5, in units of 10<sup>8</sup> m/s?
A ray of light travelling obliquely from air into glass bends ______ the normal.
questions.e: Light slows down in the optically denser glass and bends towards the normal.

questions.q: A concave lens always forms an image that is virtual, erect and ______.
questions.e: Whatever the position of the object, a concave lens gives a virtual, erect, diminished image.

questions.q: A convex lens has a power of +4 D. What is its focal length?
A concave mirror forms a real image three times the size of an object placed 10 cm from it. How far from the mirror is the image?
questions.e: m = −v ÷ u = −3, so v = 3u in size: 3 × 10 = 30 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.q: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm.
p: (a) How far from the mirror is the image formed?
(c) Is the image real or virtual?
questions.e: With u = −10 cm and f = +15 cm, 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6, so v = +6 cm (behind the mirror) and m = −v/u = 0.6.

questions.q: An object 2 cm tall is placed 15 cm in front of a concave lens of focal length 10 cm.
p: (a) How far from the lens is the image formed?
(b) What is the height of the image?
(c) Is the image real or virtual?
questions.e: With u = −15 cm and f = −10 cm, 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = −1/10 − 1/15 = −1/6, so v = −6 cm (same side as the object), m = v/u = 0.4 and the image is 2 × 0.4 = 0.8 cm tall.

questions.q: The light-sensitive screen at the back of the eye, on which the image is formed, is the ______.
questions.e: Light-sensitive cells in the retina send signals to the brain through the optic nerve.

questions.q: The ability of the eye lens to change its focal length to see near and far objects is called ______.
questions.e: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens.

questions.q: For a young adult with normal vision, the least distance of distinct vision is about ______.
questions.e: This is the near point of a normal eye; the far point is at infinity.

questions.q: Hypermetropia (far-sightedness) is corrected using a ______ lens.
questions.e: A convex lens of suitable power brings the image of a nearby object onto the retina.

questions.q: In old age, the eye lens can become milky and cloudy. This condition is called ______.
questions.e: Vision can be restored by cataract surgery.

questions.q: Stars twinkle because of atmospheric ______ of starlight.
questions.e: The changing atmosphere keeps changing the path of starlight, so the amount of light reaching the eye flickers.

questions.q: The sky appears blue because of the ______ of sunlight by very fine particles in the atmosphere.
questions.e: Fine particles scatter blue light (shorter wavelength) much more than red light.

questions.q: When white light passes through a glass prism, which colour bends the least?
questions.e: Red bends the least and violet bends the most, so the spectrum runs from red to violet.

questions.q: The sun can be seen about 2 minutes before it actually rises above the horizon. This is due to atmospheric ______.
questions.e: Refraction in the atmosphere bends sunlight so the sun appears higher than it is, giving about 2 minutes extra at sunrise and sunset.

questions.q: Danger signal lights are red because red light is scattered the ______ by fog and smoke.
questions.e: Red light has the longest wavelength, so it is scattered least and can be seen from far away.

questions.q: For a person with normal vision, where is the far point of the eye?
questions.e: A normal eye can see distant objects clearly, so its far point is at infinity.

questions.q: A hypermetropic person has a near point of 1 m and wants to read a book held at 25 cm.
p: (a) What type of lens is needed?
(b) What is the power of this lens?
questions.e: The lens must form a virtual image at 100 cm of an object at 25 cm: 1/f = 1/v − 1/u = −1/100 + 1/25 = 3/100, so f = 100/3 cm and P = +3 D.

questions.q: A rainbow is seen in the sky after a rain shower.
p: (a) It forms by dispersion of sunlight by tiny ______ in the atmosphere.
(b) Is the rainbow seen towards the sun or opposite to the sun?
questions.e: Raindrops act like small prisms: they refract, disperse and internally reflect sunlight. A rainbow always forms opposite to the sun.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric current is the ______.
questions.e: One ampere is a flow of one coulomb of charge per second.

questions.q: Which instrument is used to measure the potential difference across a component?
questions.e: A voltmeter is connected in parallel; an ammeter is connected in series.

questions.q: A charge of 10 C flows through a wire in 5 s. What is the current?
A wire's resistance is directly proportional to its length. If the length is doubled and the thickness stays the same, how many times larger does its resistance become?
questions.e: R = ρl ÷ A, so doubling l doubles R.

questions.q: Which material is used for the filament of an electric bulb because of its very high melting point?
questions.e: Tungsten melts at about 3380 °C, so it can glow white-hot without melting.

questions.q: How much work is done in moving a charge of 2 C between two points with a potential difference of 12 V?
A current of 2 A flows through a 5 Ω resistor for 10 s. How much heat is produced?
questions.e: By Joule's law, H = I²Rt = 2² × 5 × 10 = 200 J.

questions.q: How many joules make 1 kilowatt hour?
Three resistors of 3 Ω each are connected in parallel to a 6 V battery.
p: (b) What is the total current drawn from the battery?
(c) What is the current through each resistor?
questions.e: 1/R = 1/3 + 1/3 + 1/3 = 1, so R = 1 Ω; I = 6 V ÷ 1 Ω = 6 A, and each resistor has 6 V across it, so 6 ÷ 3 = 2 A.

questions.q: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines go from the ______ pole to the other pole.
questions.e: Field lines emerge from the north pole and merge at the south pole; inside the magnet they go from south to north.

questions.q: A compass needle is a small ______.
questions.e: Its north-pointing end is its north pole.

questions.q: Which scientist first noticed that an electric current in a wire deflects a nearby compass needle?
questions.e: In 1820 Hans Christian Oersted showed that electricity and magnetism are linked.

questions.q: Two magnetic field lines ______ cross each other.
questions.e: If they crossed, a compass at that point would have to point in two directions at once.

questions.q: A coil of many turns of insulated copper wire wound in the shape of a cylinder is called a ______.
questions.e: A current-carrying solenoid behaves like a bar magnet.

questions.q: Inside a long current-carrying solenoid, the magnetic field is ______.
questions.e: The parallel straight field lines inside show that the field is the same at all points.

questions.q: A strong magnet made by placing a soft iron core inside a current-carrying solenoid is called an ______.
questions.e: An electromagnet is a magnet only while current flows.

questions.q: The relative strength of a magnetic field is shown by the degree of ______ of the field lines.
questions.e: The field is stronger where the lines are closer together, as near the poles.

questions.q: The force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is largest when the current is ______ to the field.
questions.e: The force is largest when the current is at right angles to the field and zero when it is parallel.

questions.q: In Indian homes, the potential difference between the live and neutral wires is ______.
questions.e: Electricity is supplied at 220 V with a frequency of 50 Hz.

questions.q: Which safety device in a household circuit melts and breaks the circuit when too much current flows?
questions.e: A fuse protects the circuit from overloading and short circuits.

questions.q: In household wiring, the earth wire usually has ______ insulation.
questions.e: The live wire is usually red and the neutral wire black; the earth wire is green.

questions.q: What happens to the magnetic field around a straight wire when the current through it increases?
questions.e: The magnetic field is directly proportional to the current.

questions.q: A current flows through a circular loop of wire.
p: (a) Near the wire, the field lines are ______ circles.
(b) At the centre of the loop, the field lines appear as ______ lines.
(c) For a coil of n turns, the field is ______ proportional to n.
questions.e: Each part of the loop gives concentric circles; at the centre these become nearly straight, and the field adds up for every turn.
